description:
FOUND s499f (Opus, 2026-09-27) by the #2425 probe table (scratch/s499f/probes/pow.pl, powiv.pl in the s499f worktree).  PRE-EXISTING: the base extraction of main 9febb602 prints the same (pow.base identical to pow.m2); #2425's %p-pow-small arm does not touch it (its operands must already be fixnums).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    print 1e3**5, " ", "1e3"**5, " ", 1000.0**5, " ", 2.0**60, " ", "8.0"**20, " ", (10/2)**22, "\n";
    perl: 1000000000000000 1000000000000000 1000000000000000 1.15292150460685e+18 1.15292150460685e+18 2.38418579101562e+15
    PCL : 1e+15 1e+15 1e+15 1.15292150460685e+18 1.15292150460685e+18 2.38418579101562e+15
The last three agree because they leave pp_pow's integer branch anyway (power of 2 base -> NV by design; 5**22 is past the 64-bit bound).

MECHANISM: p-** takes %p-pow-int only when `(integerp na)`; perl's pp_pow asks SvIV_please_nomg, which succeeds for an NV that is an exact integer inside IV range, so `1000.0 ** 5` computes in integers and prints exactly.  PCL's to-number of "1e3" / 1e3 is the double 1000.0d0 and goes to %p-pow-float, whose 1e15 prints in %.15g.
FIX SHAPE (not built): in p-**, an operand that is a double-float with an integral value inside the IV range is handed to %p-pow-int as that integer (both operands; perl applies it to the exponent too).  Probe the breaking cases first: `2.0 ** 3` (perl 8), `(-8.0) ** 3`, `1.5 ** 2`, `1e20 ** 1` (outside IV: stays NV), NaN/Inf operands, and `-0.0 ** 3`.  Low reach: an integral float base with a result >= 1e15 is rare in everyday code.


=== WIDER FAMILY (Fable, s500, 2026-09-28; from ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s500/review/r500p-float.pl + r500p-arith.pl) ===
The same SvIV_please rule is in pp_add / pp_subtract / pp_multiply, not only pp_pow:  `print 1e15*10` -- perl 10000000000000000 (both operands integral NVs inside IV range -> IV multiply), PCL 1e+16;  `print 9007199254740993 + 0.0` -- perl 9007199254740993 (0.0 is IV-pleased to 0, the add is integer), PCL 9.00719925474099e+15 (the IV is coerced to a double and loses the last bit).  `2**62 + 2**62` agrees (9.22337203685478e+18: perl overflows to NV there).  If the `**` fix is ONE coercion helper ("an integral double inside IV range is that integer"), the + - * arms are the same helper at their slow-path entry -- size the cost on the arith bench rows (a `(= x (ftruncate x))` per double operand on the SLOW path only; the fixnum fast paths never see a double) before deciding whether the filler covers them; if not, leave them here with the numbers.  `int(1e20)` staying NV in perl (PCL prints the exact bignum) is NOT this family -- it is the documented #1513/#1515 boundless-integer model.

=== DONE (s500p) ===
Shipped in commit bb47030b: %p-iv-please on both `**` operands (an integral double of magnitude < 2^53 is that integer; fractions, NaN, Inf, >= 2^53 unchanged; -0.0 -> 0).  1e3 ** 5, "1e3" ** 5, 1000.0 ** 5 print 1000000000000000; 7.0 ** 19 is exact.  ir-spec §3.6 carries the rule.  Guard Pl/t/numeric-repr-01.t row 13 (fails on 209e7533).  Fable's r500p-pow probe: base 6 diff lines vs perl -> tree 0.  Companion op/pow.t 268/0 before == after.  Residue NOT this task: an integral ADDITION result (`1e15 + 1`) is #1369.
subject: DIVERGENCE (numeric spelling): `**` on an INTEGRAL float operand answers an NV where perl answers an integer -- `1e3 ** 5`, `"1e3" ** 5`, `1000.0 ** 5` print 1e+15 under PCL, 1000000000000000 under perl (pp_pow's SvIV_please treats an integral NV as an IV)
